Hi Elena / Tom,

Thanks again for taking time for the demo earlier — appreciate the practical questions on latency and model isolation. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the GDPR/security items you asked us to follow up on and outline next steps so your legal/privacy teams can triage: 

- SOC 2 status: Redwood is in-scope for SOC 2 Type II, last report completed Q2 2026. I can arrange an NDA + secure artifact exchange if you need the report.
- DPA: You asked for our standard DPA and a quick note on controller vs processor posture. Attached is our redwood-dpa-template.docx and a short SCC options slide.
- Controller/processor alignment: We position Redwood as processor for customer data (we run inference on your data, do not control primary purposes). If AtlasFintech requires us to take on any controller obligations for joint-determined purposes, that’s possible but requires internal legal sign-off (Ben and Marissa are CC'd).
- SCC modules: We recommended the EU Commission standard modules for processor flows, but there are a few variants depending on whether you want a slim clause set (processor-only) or a controller-processor hybrid. See attached Redwood_SCC_options.pdf.

Requested next steps from our side:
1) Elena/Tom: please confirm the privacy contact who will receive the SOC 2 artifact and the DPA redlines (if any).
2) AtlasFintech: if you have a checklist (your privacy intake workbook), attach it and we'll map items against our controls.
3) Redwood (Marissa/Ben): if AtlasFintech asks for controller-side commitments beyond a standard processor DPA, Ben will lead the legal assessment and escalate to product as needed.

I attached a short "Atlas_fin_privacy_checklist.xlsx" you can use to mark priority items — fill in the right-hand column and we’ll respond in one pass.

If useful, we can schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call early next week.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Jordan / Elena / Tom,

Thanks for the clear thread. Quick legal/controls note from our side:

- SOC 2: happy to provide the Type II report. Jordan, sending the secure portal link to you now (separate email). Elena: once we receive a signed NDA I'll provision access.
- DPA template: starting point is fine. For AtlasFintech's use-case (inference-only, Redwood not initiating processing purposes) we recommend the processor-centric SCC module (processor-to-controller flow) unless Atlas insists on custom joint-responsibility clauses.
- Subprocessors: we publish our subprocessors list and will include the most common infra and monitoring subprocessors; we can provide a snapshot as of the date of the SOC 2 report.
- Embeddings retention: Redwood offers configurable retention and an option to opt-out of persistent embedding storage — we can document the default and a retention policy to put into the DPA.
